findings.message:
[P1] Preserve legacy agent tokens lacking authorizationVersion

Existing `AgentTokenRecord` values predate this field and have no `authorizationVersion`; when the user is still at the default version `0`, this strict comparison evaluates `undefined !== 0` and treats the token as stale even though `authorizationVersionOf` normalizes both missing versions to `0`. `getAgentTokenBySecret` then deletes the retained opaque token and its exchange returns 401, breaking existing agent tokens; normalize the record version before comparing (as `handleAgentTokenExchange` already does).

src/auth_store.ts:1270-1270

summary: The change implements authorization-version revocation and the required administrator-demotion test, but it silently invalidates every pre-existing agent token that lacks the new version field.

evidence: `signAccessToken` adds the normalized current `authorizationVersion` to every issued JWT (src/token_service.ts:149), and bearer verification rejects a token whose version differs from the current user's (src/token_service.ts:218-220).

The stored user version is advanced on administrator and scope edits (src/auth_store.ts:784-802), password and passkey reset paths (src/auth_store.ts:688-734, 736-766, 957-993), logout (src/passport.ts:1266), and agent-token revocation (src/auth_store.ts:1311-1334); deletion makes verification fail because the user lookup returns null.
`GET /api/auth/session/me` is documented as the introspection path and verifies bearer version through `requireClaims`, returning 401 for stale tokens (README.md:147-150; src/passport.ts:1173-1194).
The worker-runtime test logs in an administrator, demotes that account, and asserts the previously valid bearer receives 401 (tests/worker_runtime.mjs:948-981).
